title: GravityZone high severity alerts
volume: None on a normal day. Each blocked attack or High incident makes one detection, in the computer's case.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Four custom detection rules for Bitdefender GravityZone, on the third-party alert records the library's GravityZone parsers write from its push events. They make a detection when GravityZone's ransomware mitigation acts, when its EDR raises a High incident, when Advanced Anti-Exploit blocks an exploit, and when Sandbox Analyzer finds a file malicious. Each rule matches sensor type Bitdefender GravityZone only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's Bitdefender GravityZone parsers and point GravityZone's event push service at HTTP Ingest first, as the parser entry says, then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive. The push settings' subscribeToEventTypes must include the modules these rules read.

How it works:
- The parsers write GravityZone's module, such as ransomware-mitigation, as the alert category, and the computer as the target host.
- GravityZone rates only incidents, so the parsers set ransomware mitigation, Anti-Exploit and Sandbox Analyzer to High. The incident rule takes incidents and extended incidents GravityZone rates High.
- Advanced Threat Control blocks, Network Attack Defense and Antiphishing aren't taken: GravityZone makes those every day as it blocks things, and an incident follows when one matters.
- Antimalware detections go to the Antivirus schema, which these rules don't read.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 8 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about a minute. The lines went in 16 to 23 minutes after the rules were made, and every rule fired on the first send.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on any of the samples, the Antivirus records included.
- The lines went to HTTP Ingest one per request, as GravityZone's push service sends them, and each was stored as one record and parsed.

Known gaps:
- An extended incident names no computer, so its detection carries no host name and the case rule doesn't take it.
- When GravityZone batches several events in one POST, only the first is normalized, as the parser entry says.
